Connect only this iCESugar when programming: its programmer can't tell iCESugar boards apart, so the engine refuses when another board with the same USB IDs, such as an iCESugar-Pro, is connected.
configurations.maintainer_notes: iCESugar boards share USB IDs and product name. The serial number's first 4 characters are the board ID, as icesprog's source reads it: 0700 iCESugar, 0710 iCESugar-Pro, 0720 iCESugar-nano. 0700 also seen in a real iCESugar v1.5's USB log.

configurations.user_notes: Its USB filter matches any device with an FTDI FT232H chip.
configurations.maintainer_notes: Programmed with iceprog through its FTDI FT232H chip, as the board maker's examples do (github.com/skerr92/ice5lp4k_examples). It was defined with icesprog, which can only reach MuseLab's iCELink, not an FTDI chip. Not tried on hardware.

configurations.user_notes: Programming needs the board in its bootloader (DFU) mode; on many boards, hold its button while plugging it in. Its USB filter also matches the other OrangeCrab r0.2 size (25K or 85K), so the engine can't tell which one is connected.

Programming writes the FPGA's SRAM, so the design is lost at power-off. Its USB filter matches every ULX3S size and any device with an FTDI FT231X chip.
configurations.maintainer_notes: Moved from fujprog, which is legacy, to openFPGALoader's ulx3s board, writing SRAM as fujprog did. Not tried on hardware.
